title: Active Nav Class
prompt: A React navigation link needs a className based on the current path. Write a helper that returns "nav-item active" when href equals currentPath and "nav-item" otherwise.

explanation.beginner:
Example: activeNavClass("/problems", "/problems") produces "nav-item active". Evaluate the selection rule for every record and preserve the qualifying values in the required order.

Compare “leaves inactive links plain”: input ["/courses","/problems"] produces "nav-item". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Evaluate the selection rule for every record and preserve the qualifying values in the required order.

Tempting mistake: Selecting a display position after a list changes can identify the wrong item. Use the domain key when matching two collections.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “leaves inactive links plain”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
